what: Kymera Therapeutics designs drugs that destroy disease-causing proteins rather than merely blocking them, using the cell's own disposal machinery. Its lead programmes target inflammatory diseases.
customers: Pharmaceutical partners funding its programmes, and eventually patients with inflammatory and autoimmune conditions.
money: payments from Sanofi and other partners
moat: A protein degradation platform with real clinical data behind it, in a field where very few companies have taken a degrader into late-stage trials.
risks: A $349M net loss on $102M of revenue: this is a research company, not a business yet
100 times sales, and the revenue is partner payments that end when a partnership does
No approved product, so everything depends on trial results that could fail
opportunities: $848M of cash against $79M of debt, enough to fund several years of trials
Analysts see about 22% upside, with 23 covering the stock
Its oral inflammatory degraders target conditions currently treated with injected biologics, a very large market
watch: Clinical trial readouts on the lead inflammatory programmes.
